title: Probabilistic fallback simulator + playbook (latency / cost / reliability)
content:
Goal: capture a compact, operational playbook + lightweight simulator for choosing route targets (host + model variant + region) under competing objectives: P95 latency, per-request unit cost, and failure/retry risk. We want something that SREs/Platform can run locally or in CI to validate rollout policies and to sanity-check policy parameter changes before fleet-wide publish.

Motivation / intuition:
- Observed behavior: cost-optimized routes sometimes push high tail latency during regional spikes; naive fallbacks that always prefer cheaper variants cause SLO violations.
- Idea: move from hard-rule fallbacks to a probabilistic decision layer that uses an explicit risk budget and expected-utility calculation per-request.

High-level design constraints:
- Must be implementable in control plane with O(1) per-request scoring (no heavy per-request lookups).
- Uses a small set of online signals: recent P95 by region/model (sliding window), error-rate, queue-length proxy, and budget counters (per-customer risk budget).
- Deterministic-ish in steady-state: if metric signals are stable, decisions should be stable to ease debugging.

Core concepts (vocabulary):
- candidate: tuple (region, host-pool, model-variant)
- score(candidate) = alpha * latency_score + beta * cost_score + gamma * risk_score
- risk_budget(customer): remaining allowed expected-fails for a time window (eg daily) before escalations
- fallback-temper: a tunable that controls exploration of cheaper/less-reliable candidates (0.0 conservative -> 1.0 aggressive)

Scoring sketches (working):
- latency_score: normalized inverse of recent median latency (higher = better). Use clipped P50/P95 mixture: L = 0.7 * norm(P50) + 0.3 * norm(P95_tail_penalty)
- cost_score: negative normalized cost per effective token (higher = cheaper). Normalize across model variants in the catalog.
- risk_score: estimate of expected additional retries if chosen. Derived from recent success_rate and queue proxies; higher success => higher risk_score. We compute expected additional end-to-end latency multiplier from typical retry patterns.

Probabilistic selection algorithm (pseudo):
- Given candidate set C and customer with risk_budget R:
  1) compute raw_score[c] for c in C (linear combo with weights tuned by policy)
  2) transform to utility U[c] = exp(raw_score / T) (softmax-style, T = temperature derived from fallback-temper)
  3) sample a candidate with probability proportional to U[c], but enforce hard constraints: exclude any candidate whose recent error_rate > threshold_for_customer_tier
  4) if sampled candidate would exceed R (expected extra failures > R), fall back to next-best deterministic pick (argmax raw_score) and decrement R appropriately

Why sampling?
- Introduces controlled exploration so we don’t permanently bias away from candidates that occasionally recover (helps cost optimization).
- Avoids synchronized switching waves across traffic when a candidate toggles between marginally-better/worse due to noise.

Decision tree (operator-view) - ASCII sketch for runbook:
  [Start request]
       |
       v
  Check hard-blockers: (region blackout, host pool degraded?) -> if yes, route to global-fallback 
       | no
       v
  Gather signals: P95_region, queue_len, token_estimate, customer_risk_budget R
       |
       v
  Score candidates -> rank top-3 -> apply temperature-> sample -> got candidate X?
       |
       v
  If expected_retries(X) > R -> mark X as risky, pick deterministic best non-risky
       |
       v
  Emit route decision + annotations (why chosen, signal snapshot)

Simulation notes + example results (toy workload):
- Setup: synthetic 10k req/min, three regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-south), 4 model variants (large-fast-expensive, med-balanced, small-cheap, quantized-cheaper-but-unreliable).
- SLO target: P95 < 250ms global. Cost metric: normalized units / req. Risk budget per-customer window = 0.5 expected fails/day.

Baseline heuristic A (always choose cheapest subject to >95% success): 
- P95 observed: 310ms (miss)
- Cost units: 0.45 (good)
- Failure spikes correlated with regional queue surges.

Probabilistic policy P (alpha=0.5 latency, beta=0.3 cost, gamma=0.2 risk, fallback-temper=0.25):
- P95 observed: 235ms (within SLO)
- Cost units: 0.62 (higher cost)
- Customer-visible error rate: modest reduction vs A

Aggressive-explore policy E (higher fallback-temper=0.8):
- P95: 255ms (borderline)
- Cost units: 0.48 (better than P)
- Observed oscillation across model variants during regional transient windows (more debugging noise)

Interpretation: the probabilistic policy gives a favorable latency win at the expense of increased unit cost; temperature trade controls exploration + operational noise. We should default to conservative temperature for high-SLA customers and more aggressive for low-SLA or cost-conscious customers.

Operational telemetry and observability hooks we need:
- Decision annotation emitted with each request: chosen_candidate, raw_scores map, sampled_flag(true|false), risk_budget_state, signals_snapshot (P95, qlen, success_rate)
- Aggregates: fraction sampled vs deterministic, cost delta vs baseline, P95 delta per-customer, retry-contribution to P95, sample-induced variance.
- Alerting: if sampling fraction > X and P95 trending up -> auto-rollback sampling temperature by 2x; if region error_rate > threshold -> hard block region in control plane.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Synchronized sampling causing flash-flock to a single candidate. Mitigation: use per-shard jitter seed and small-memory deterministic shard-based hashing to decorrelate draws.
- Stale signals leading to bad picks. Mitigation: signal TTL and emergency revert to deterministic argmax when key signals are older than N seconds.
- Risk budget exhaustion on a critical customer. Mitigation: per-customer escalation, plus fallback to reserved low-latency capacity or priority routing lane.

Implementation notes for control plane:
- Scoring happens in control plane service (stateless) using cached per-candidate metrics stored in small in-memory store (ttl 10s) synced from TSDB via push stream.
- Sampling decision should attach a stable decision-id so SRE can correlate logs and traces.
- Expose simple policy config YAML: weights, temperature_by_tier, hard_thresholds, per-customer-reset-window. Example snippet (informal):
  policy:
    weights: {latency: 0.5, cost: 0.3, risk: 0.2}
    temp_by_tier: {gold: 0.15, standard: 0.25, economy: 0.6}
    hard_block_error_rate: 0.12

Playbook steps for policy changes (quick):
1) Run simulator with current traffic replay (10m window) -> get delta matrix (P95, cost, errors)
2) If P95 increases > 5% for gold tier, abort and lower temp
3) Canary: enable sampling for 1% traffic, monitor sampled_fraction and P95 for 30m
4) If stable, ramp to 10% then to 50% with checks at each step
5) On unexpected regressions, auto-rollback to previous version and open incident ticket

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute expected_retries more accurately when retries may be routed to different candidate pools? (propagation of drawn sampling semantics)
- Formalize risk_budget per-customer: should it be based on revenue or SLA tier? (propose: revenue-weighted budget)
- Add a mode to bias sampling away from variance-inducing candidates when global traffic variance > threshold (detect systemic noise).
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations: can we auto-tune weights alpha/beta/gamma per-customer using historical cost vs latency Pareto frontier?

Next actions (short):
- Evan: prototype the simulator harness as a replay-capable CLI (github PR stub linked above) (ETA 2w)
- Lara: draft policy YAML + default temps by tier and put into policy repo (ETA 1w)
- Mateo: add decision annotation protobuf and open design PR for control-plane integration (ETA 2w)
- Priya (me): schedule playtest run with sample customer workloads next Wed; prepare rollback plan and dashboards.

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep sampling seed per-shard derived from request id prefix to reduce cross-shard syncs.
- Consider a simple momentum term in raw_score to avoid flip-flop when scores hover.
- Document example incident timeline for risk_budget breach and escalation path.

References and quick links:
- Routing sim repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/pull/56
- Confluence design stub: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-958

End of doc.
